name: Separate in time
q: Can the two opposite demands be satisfied at different times?
how: Have the thing be one way now and the other way later. Most 'we need both' problems in a service dissolve the moment you ask when each is needed.
mfg: A jig that is loose during loading and rigid during machining.
svc: Underwriting must be fast and thorough: decide fast now on the 80% that fit the rules, and thoroughly later on the sample and the exceptions.

name: Separate in space
q: Can the two opposite demands live in different places, or different parts of the system?
how: Let one part or one location be one way, and another be the opposite. Nothing says the whole system has to have a single setting.
mfg: A drill bit hard at the tip and tough in the shank.
svc: Service must be standardised and personal: standardise the back office completely, personalise only the customer-facing edge.

name: Separate on condition
q: Can the two opposite demands apply under different conditions — for different cases, customers or triggers?
how: Make the behaviour depend on a condition, so the system is one way when the condition holds and the other way when it does not.
mfg: A filter that passes liquid but blocks solids.
svc: Refunds must be instant and controlled: instant under £50 or for customers with clean history, reviewed otherwise.

name: Separate between the parts and the whole
q: Can the demand be true of the whole system but not of its parts — or the reverse?
how: Move up or down a level. Individual parts can be rigid while the assembly is flexible; individual people can be specialists while the team is a generalist.
mfg: A bicycle chain: every link is rigid, the chain as a whole is flexible.
svc: Teams must be specialist and able to cover anything: every individual is a deep specialist, while the team as a unit covers the full range.
